content.text:
Oracle Cites ‘Force Majeure’ to Shield Itself on Controversial Data Center: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Oracle sent the Project Jupiter developer a force majeure notice and was seeking to defer payments if the campus missed its 2028 target, rather than exit as tenant. The report does not reproduce the notice itself. (time=2026-09-24T12:25:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Oracle, BorderPlex, and Bloom Energy to Power Project Jupiter with Cleaner, Water-Efficient Fuel Cell Technology: Oracle said Project Jupiter would use up to 2.45 GW of installed Bloom fuel-cell capacity, replacing previously planned gas turbines and diesel generators. The release said construction was continuing on schedule as of Apr 27. (time=2026-04-27; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Bloom Energy and Oracle Expand Strategic Partnership to Deploy up to 2.8 GW to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Build-Out: Bloom said the expanded master services agreement supported up to 2.8 GW, with an initial 1.2 GW contracted and deployment underway across Oracle projects in the U.S. The release did not identify that initial contracted capacity as Jupiter-specific. (time=2026-04-13; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
